advances: For an arbitrary fixed positive all-double normal-fan stratum, this gives the complete exact linearized release system directly from the clipping code, proves its rational Farkas alternative, and expands the dual as a common-plane support-contact stress identity. A dual stress at every realization blocks every piecewise-rational release path, while absence of the stress is equivalent to one explicit projected cone inequality. Thus the one numerical prototype is not used as evidence for the general case: the remaining geometric step is exactly the uniform projected release inequality displayed below. The proof also gives the general exact first-event rule for any rational motion once such a motion has been constructed.
author: mp_r127_rank2_general_release
proof:
The only point requiring care in defining \(E\) and \(G\) is that clipped areas and the capacity must be differentiated on the actual fixed code, rather than replaced by abstract cell variables. If an edge with endpoints \(u,v\) meets a fixed affine cut \(\ell=0\) and \(\ell(v)-\ell(u)\neq0\), its intersection is
\[
\mathsf i_\ell(u,v)
=\frac{\ell(v)u-\ell(u)v}{\ell(v)-\ell(u)}.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus every vertex of every clipped chamber polygon is either an original polygon vertex, a fixed cut-cut intersection, or a rational function (6) of two original vertices. If \(w_0(x),\ldots,w_{m-1}(x)\) are the cyclic vertices of one clipped cell on the fixed code, its signed area is
\[
\mathcal A(x)=\frac12\sum_{\nu=0}^{m-1}
[w_\nu(x),w_{\nu+1}(x)]
\tag{7}
\]
and its exact differential is
\[
D\mathcal A(x)[\xi]
=\frac12\sum_{\nu=0}^{m-1}
\left(
[Dw_\nu(x)[\xi],w_{\nu+1}(x)]
+[w_\nu(x),Dw_{\nu+1}(x)[\xi]]
\right).
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (6)-(8), with the quotient rule, give every chamber-area row of \(E\) without an approximation.

The same argument applies to \(\mathscr C\). On a fixed visible-fan and charging code, each of its polygonal vertices is an original vertex, an edge-cut intersection of the form (6), or the intersection of two moving supporting lines. The latter is rational by the two-by-two Cramer formula while the defining determinant stays nonzero. Shoelace formula (7) therefore makes \(\mathscr C\) rational and (8) gives its exact row.

The remaining rows are polynomial. For a persistent cut incidence, the row is \(D(\ell(v))\). For a persistent shared ray, differentiation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
D[a_{i+1}-a_i,q_{j+1}-q_j][\xi]
={}&[\dot a_{i+1}-\dot a_i,q_{j+1}-q_j]\\
&+[a_{i+1}-a_i,\dot q_{j+1}-\dot q_j].
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
For containment,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D\eta_{sj}(x)[\xi]
={}&[\dot k_{s+1}-\dot k_s,b_j-k_s]\\
&+[k_{s+1}-k_s,\dot b_j-\dot k_s],
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\dot b_j=\frac{\dot a_{\iota_0(j)}+\dot q_{\iota_2(j)}}2.
\tag{10}
\]
Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D\Delta_r(x)[\xi]
={}&[\dot a_r-\dot a_{r-1},a_{r+1}-a_r]\\
&+[a_r-a_{r-1},\dot a_{r+1}-\dot a_r].
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (8)-(11) are the complete linearized system generation rule for any fixed code.

To check the crossings, write every endpoint cap and middle cap as the sum of its individual sign-cell areas. In the convention of accepted fact `89563f2f27529ab0`, the \(i\)-th crossing functional is
\[
\sum_{J\ni i}P_J+\sum_{G\ni i}Q_G+\sum_{G\ni i}R_G
-\frac29\left(\sum_JP_J+\sum_GQ_G+\sum_GR_G\right).
\tag{12}
\]
It is therefore a fixed linear combination of the individual chamber-area coordinates. Every velocity in \(\ker E\) annihilates (12). Appending the three crossing rows changes neither \(\ker E\) nor system (1).

We now prove (2) without a numerical LP. Let
\[
\mathcal K=\{\xi:E\xi=0,\ G\xi\geq0\}.
\]
If (D) holds, then for every \(\xi\in\mathcal K\),
\[
\mathcal R\xi
=y^{\mathsf T}E\xi-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G\xi
=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G\xi\leq0.
\]
Hence (P) is impossible.

Conversely, suppose (D) fails. The set
\[
\mathcal D=\{y^{\mathsf T}E-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G:
y\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{rows}(E)},\
\lambda\geq0\}
\]
is a closed polyhedral cone: it is the sum of the row space of \(E\) and the finitely generated cone spanned by the negatives of the rows of \(G\). Since \(\mathcal R\notin\mathcal D\), finite-dimensional strong separation gives a vector \(\xi\) such that
\[
d\xi\leq0\quad(d\in\mathcal D),\qquad
\mathcal R\xi>0.
\]
Both \(y^{\mathsf T}E\) and \(-y^{\mathsf T}E\) belong to \(\mathcal D\), so \(E\xi=0\). Also \(-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G\in\mathcal D\) for every \(\lambda\geq0\), so \(G\xi\geq0\). Scaling \(\xi\) by the positive number \(1/(\mathcal R\xi)\) proves (P). Thus exactly one alternative holds.

When the data are rational, (P) is a nonempty rational polyhedron and hence contains a rational point. Likewise (D) is a nonempty rational polyhedron in \((y,\lambda)\) and hence contains a rational point. This proves exact-certificate rationality.

For (3), the \(a_r\)-gradient of \(-\Delta_r\), obtained from (11), is
\[
\nabla_{a_r}(-\Delta_r)=J(a_{r+1}-a_{r-1}).
\]
From (10),
\[
\nabla_{a_r}\eta_{sj}
=\frac12J(k_{s+1}-k_s)
\quad\text{when }\iota_0(j)=r,
\]
and it is zero otherwise. Taking the \(a_r\)-block of (2) gives (3); taking all coordinate blocks gives the full equilibrium stress. Equation (4) is the already proved implication of (2).

Substitute \(\xi=Nz\). System (1), before normalization, becomes
\[
\overline Gz\geq0,\qquad
\overline{\mathcal R}z>0.
\]
Applying the just-proved alternative in the reduced coordinates shows that this system is feasible exactly when there is no \(\lambda\geq0\) with
\[
\overline{\mathcal R}=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}\overline G,
\]
which is exactly (5). This proves both the claimed minimal projected condition and the assertion that its failure is the exact dual obstruction.

Now let \(x(t)\) be a feasible piecewise \(C^1\) motion and assume a dual certificate exists at every point, using the active contacts there. At every differentiability point, \(DF(x(t))x'(t)=0\). A contact slack which is zero at an interior time and remains nonnegative has derivative zero there; at a one-sided initial time its derivative is nonnegative. Monotonicity of \(\mathscr C\) gives \(D\mathscr C(x(t))x'(t)\geq0\) at every differentiability point. Therefore (4) gives
\[
-\frac{d}{dt}\Delta_r(x(t))\leq0
\]
on each smooth piece. Hence \(\Delta_r\) is nondecreasing and cannot reach zero from a positive initial value. This proves the uniform path obstruction.

For the event assertion, (6)-(11) and the analogous two-line intersection formulas show that every code-defining quantity is rational along a rational motion. Factoring its exact order at \(t=0\) determines whether a base equality persists or immediately opens into one of its two signs. After this one-sided initialization and cancellation of functions which vanish identically, every remaining numerator and denominator is a nonzero univariate polynomial and therefore has finitely many roots on the bounded parameter interval. If this finite family has a positive root or pole, its least one is exact and leaves every prescribed one-sided sign unchanged beforehand. A zero of \(\Delta_r\) makes \(a_r\) collinear with its neighbors; convexity and the unchanged cyclic edge order place it on their segment, so deleting it leaves the convex set and all its chamber areas, crossings, contacts, and capacity unchanged. Any other first zero or pole is precisely the corresponding declared boundary event. If there is no positive root or pole, no event occurs on the chosen interval. This proves the first-event rule, including contacts which become strict immediately after \(t=0\).

The argument deliberately stops at (5). A feasible direction at one rational realization does not prove (5) for every realization, and a tangent direction alone does not supply a piecewise-rational curve on a singular equality fiber. Establishing (5) uniformly, together with rational integration on each resulting regular stratum, is the remaining general geometric work before an iteration to a three-side terminal polygon can be claimed.
statement:
Write \([u,v]=u_1v_2-u_2v_1\) and \(Ju=(-u_2,u_1)\). Fix a positive all-double normal-fan stratum with counterclockwise vertex lists
\[
A_0=(a_0,\ldots,a_{n_0-1}),\qquad
A_2=(q_0,\ldots,q_{n_2-1}),\qquad
K=(k_0,\ldots,k_{n_K-1}).
\]
The stratum fixes:

1. the clipping order of every \(P,Q,R\) chamber cut out by the three fixed affine cutting lines;
2. the merged-fan map
\[
b_j=\frac{a_{\iota_0(j)}+q_{\iota_2(j)}}2
\]
for the vertices of \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\);
3. every persistent zero-coordinate vertex-cut incidence and every persistent shared normal-fan ray; and
4. the visible-fan and charging code used to compute the zero-charge capacity \(\mathscr C\).

Let \(x\in\mathbb R^{2(n_0+n_2+n_K)}\) be the vector of all vertex coordinates. On this stratum, let \(F(x)\) be the following complete equality vector:

* every individual \(P,Q,R\) chamber area minus its fixed value;
* every retained zero-coordinate incidence \(\ell(v)=0\);
* every persistent shared-ray equation
\[
[a_{i+1}-a_i,q_{j+1}-q_j]=0;
\]
* every other persistent vertex-cut, repeated-vertex, or collinearity equality declared by the fixed stratum code.

The three crossing equalities may be appended to \(F\), but they add no condition once all individual chamber areas are fixed. Let
\[
E(x)=DF(x).
\]

For every supporting edge \(e_s=k_{s+1}-k_s\) of \(K\) and every merged-fan vertex \(b_j\), orient the containment slack as
\[
\eta_{sj}(x)=[e_s,b_j-k_s]\geq0.
\]
Let \(I(x)=\{(s,j):\eta_{sj}(x)=0\}\). Let \(G(x)\) have the rows
\[
D\eta_{sj}(x)\quad((s,j)\in I(x)),\qquad D\mathscr C(x),
\]
and, if the stratum starts on any other feasibility boundary which is required to remain feasible rather than being declared an immediate stopping event, append the differential of that active nonnegative slack. Strict convexity, strict cut signs, nonzero clipping denominators, and strict noncontacts need no linearized row because their first zero is a declared boundary event.

For an unmarked genuine vertex \(a_r\), put
\[
\Delta_r(x)=[a_r-a_{r-1},a_{r+1}-a_r]>0,\qquad
\mathcal R(x)=-D\Delta_r(x).
\]
Then the exact first-order contact-release system is
\[
E(x)\xi=0,\qquad G(x)\xi\geq0,\qquad
\mathcal R(x)\xi\geq1.
\tag{1}
\]
Exactly one of the following alternatives holds:

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{(P)}&\text{system (1) has a solution};\\[1mm]
\mathrm{(D)}&\text{there are }y\text{ and }\lambda\geq0\text{ such that}\\
&\displaystyle
\mathcal R(x)=y^{\mathsf T}E(x)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G(x).
\end{array}
\tag{2}
\]
If \(x\) and all fixed cuts are rational, both a primal certificate in (P), when it exists, and a dual certificate in (D), when it exists, may be chosen rational.

The contact part of (2) is an exact common-plane stress. In particular, if \(\lambda_{\mathscr C}\) is the capacity multiplier, the \(a_r\)-coordinate block of (2) is
\[
J(a_{r+1}-a_{r-1})
=
\sum_\alpha y_\alpha\nabla_{a_r}F_\alpha
-\frac12
\sum_{\substack{(s,j)\in I(x)\\\iota_0(j)=r}}
\lambda_{sj}J(k_{s+1}-k_s)
-\lambda_{\mathscr C}\nabla_{a_r}\mathscr C,
\tag{3}
\]
when there is no appended active feasibility row involving \(a_r\); in the general case its term \(-\lambda_\beta\nabla_{a_r}h_\beta\) is appended to the right-hand side. There is an analogous exact balance at every \(a_i,q_j,k_s\). For every velocity preserving the equalities and pointing into all active contact and capacity halfspaces, a dual stress gives the common-plane inequality
\[
-D\Delta_r(x)[\xi]
=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}G(x)\xi\leq0.
\tag{4}
\]

Let the columns of \(N(x)\) be any basis of \(\ker E(x)\), and set
\[
\overline{\mathcal R}(x)=\mathcal R(x)N(x),\qquad
\overline G(x)=G(x)N(x).
\]
The exact smallest remaining first-order geometric assertion needed for general release at \(x\) is the projected release inequality
\[
\overline{\mathcal R}(x)\notin
-\operatorname{cone}\{\text{rows of }\overline G(x)\}.
\tag{5}
\]
It is equivalent to (P), and its failure is exactly the dual obstruction (D). Consequently, if (D) holds at every realization in a stratum component, with the active rows taken at that realization, then \(\Delta_r\) is nondecreasing along every feasible piecewise \(C^1\), hence every feasible piecewise-rational, motion in that component whose capacity is nondecreasing. Such a component admits no contact-release motion deleting \(a_r\).

Finally, suppose a rational motion \(x(t)\), \(0\leq t\leq T<\infty\), satisfying the exact equalities has been constructed. First factor the exact power of \(t\) from every code function which vanishes at \(t=0\). A function whose first nonzero coefficient points into its allowed strict side gives the one-sided code on \(0<t\ll1\); a function which vanishes identically remains a persistent equality. On that one-sided fixed code, all chamber areas, contact slacks, the capacity, and all code-defining quantities are rational functions of \(t\). If a positive boundary event occurs in \((0,T]\), it is exactly the least positive zero or pole among the finite list consisting of:

* polygon turn determinants;
* vertex-cut signs, moving edge-cut denominators, and edge-through-cut-intersection determinants;
* cross-fan determinants;
* support-contact slacks;
* visible-fan and charging determinants for \(\mathscr C\); and
* \(\Delta_r\).

Before that parameter value the one-sided code is unchanged. At it, either \(\Delta_r=0\), so the collinear vertex may be deleted without changing the polygon, or one or more explicitly identified members of the list give the declared boundary event. If the list has no positive zero or pole in \((0,T]\), there is no event on that interval. This event rule does not itself assert (5), rational integrability of (1), or iteration to a three-side terminal polygon.
